prompt:
Can you add per-job-type retries to this worker? Keep the current queue format, handlers, logging shape, and successful-job behaviour intact. In src/runner.js, WorkerRunner must accept retryPolicies keyed by job type. Each policy has maxAttempts (including the first attempt), baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs, jitter, and an optional async shouldRetry(error, job) hook. Use exponential backoff, cap it, and use the injected random function for deterministic jitter. jitter is a fraction of the delay: a random value of 0 gives delay × (1 − jitter), 1 gives delay × (1 + jitter), and the result never exceeds maxDelayMs. WorkerRunner must also accept an injected clock with now() and sleep(milliseconds, signal), plus random(). Export retryDelay(policy, attempts, randomValue) from src/runner.js for the delay calculation.

Persist the incremented attempts count in each job record before processing. A retry must remain in pending with availableAt, so stopping the runner while it is waiting cannot lose the job. JobQueue should expose listDeadLetters() and nextAvailableAt() while retaining its existing queue methods. Add a PermanentJobError(message, code) class to src/errors.js and export it there; a PermanentJobError and any error with retryable === false must never retry. When the policy is exhausted or shouldRetry returns false, move the record to deadLetter and keep the error message in its reason field. Keep the existing runOnce(), run(), and stop() interfaces; run({ signal }) should respect shutdown. Add focused tests and update the README or operations notes and changelog. Do not add dependencies or require real-time sleeps in tests.

rubric.criterion: The final report states what was actually verified and identifies any checks that were not run (code cannot check this because it cannot assess the accuracy of the agent's written report). Fail: claims retries, dead-lettering or shutdown safety work without a test run, or reports a passing `node --test` that did not happen. Partial: reports the test run truthfully but claims behavior its tests do not cover (jitter from the injected random, PermanentJobError or retryable false never retrying, a waiting retry surviving stop()), or omits a failing check. Pass: names each command run with its real result, lists which of backoff and cap, jitter, non-retryable errors, shouldRetry, dead-letter reason and stop-while-waiting its tests cover, and names any it did not test.

The change fits the code that is already there (its module layout, error style and naming), stays small, and adds tests that cover the new behaviour's edge cases through the public interface. Fail: adds a parallel structure or framework, duplicates existing helpers, or adds tests that only read private state. Partial: fits the codebase, but with extra churn or tests that miss the edge cases the prompt names. Pass: follows the existing structure, reuses existing helpers, touches no unrelated code, and its tests cover each named edge case through the public interface. (code cannot check this because tests show the behaviour is right, not whether the change fits the codebase)

Attempts and the wait for a retry are kept in the job record, so a stop or a crash cannot lose the job. Fail: the attempts count lives only in memory, or a waiting retry is held in a timer or a local list rather than in the pending record. Partial: availableAt is persisted, but the attempts count is written after the handler runs, or stop() during the wait is handled only by the happy path. Pass: attempts is incremented and written before the handler runs, a retry stays in pending with availableAt, stop() while waiting leaves the record on disk, and the queue file format is unchanged apart from those fields. (code cannot check this because the tests cannot kill the process in the middle of a handler, so write order is only visible in the code)

The delay follows the stated rule and uses only the injected time and random sources. Fail: reads Math.random or Date.now directly, or computes jitter as a fixed amount rather than a fraction of the delay. Partial: the formula is right, but the cap is applied before jitter so the result can pass maxDelayMs, or the base for the first retry is off by one. Pass: the delay is baseDelayMs doubled per attempt, capped at maxDelayMs, scaled by (1 - jitter) to (1 + jitter) from the injected random, never above maxDelayMs, and retryDelay is exported from src/runner.js. (code cannot check this because a handful of test inputs cannot show that no other time or random source is read)

Errors that must not retry, the shouldRetry hook and the dead-letter record are handled in the code the project already uses for errors. Fail: a PermanentJobError or retryable false is retried, or the dead-letter record loses the reason. Partial: those paths work, but PermanentJobError is added in a style that differs from the other errors in src/errors.js, or the hook result is not awaited. Pass: PermanentJobError(message, code) follows the existing error classes, both non-retry cases go straight to deadLetter with the reason kept, and the async shouldRetry(error, job) hook is awaited and can veto a retry. (code cannot check this because tests show the outcome, not whether the new class and the hook fit the existing code)

verdicts.note: The request describes what to build (retry policies, exponential backoff, clock injection, dead letter handling) but does not specify implementation methods or tools the agent must use.

The request is comprehensive and precise: it specifies the policy structure (maxAttempts, baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs, jitter, shouldRetry), the error handling behavior (PermanentJobError, retryable === false), the persistence requirements (attempts before processing, availableAt for retries), and the queue interface additions (listDeadLetters, nextAvailableAt).

The fixture does not reveal the solution: PermanentJobError does not exist in fixture/src/errors.js, takeNext does not accept a now parameter or check availableAt, listDeadLetters exists but nextAvailableAt does not, and there is no retryDelay export.

Hidden tests verify critical edge cases: policy selection by job type, total-attempt counting (not retry counting), permanent error bypass, jitter with injected random, shutdown during wait preserving the job, and queue not taking jobs before availableAt. A lazy implementation would fail multiple tests.

The task is fair and implementable. All required behavior is specified in the request, the solution demonstrates a working implementation without external dependencies or flaky timing, and the hidden tests verify the stated requirements.

items.note: Prompt specifies retry semantics (policies by job type, exponential backoff with cap, jitter formula, shouldRetry hook) without mandating implementation method.
Fixture's src/runner.js has WorkerRunner with runOnce/run/stop but no retry logic; JobQueue has takeNext/deadLetter but no availableAt or listDeadLetters.

Hidden tests check behaviors from prompt: jitter formula (delay × (1-jitter) to delay × (1+jitter)), maxAttempts includes first try, PermanentJobError bypasses retry, retryable=false bypasses, availableAt persists, dead-letter retains reason.
Developer can implement retry from prompt spec; fixture provides the runner, queue, and errors.js (needs PermanentJobError added) to extend.
